chunks: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

key_terms.الْكُحْلُ: Kohl (eyeliner), a cosmetic powder used for the eyes.
key_terms.يُعْذِبُ: Freshens or makes sweet (in taste or smell).

ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of using kohl according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the term 'yu'adhib' is interpreted by Shia scholars as enhancing or sweetening the breath, highlighting the cosmetic practice of kohl as a means of personal hygiene and pleasantness. This ruling reflects the broader Islamic emphasis on cleanliness (taharah) and removing unpleasant odors, which is considered an act of worship when done for the sake of pleasing Allah and others. The brevity of the hadith underscores the practical, everyday nature of the guidance, linking physical grooming to spiritual and social well-being.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hammad Bin Isa, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
en.sarwar: 5. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ibn Faddal from Hammad ibn ‘Isa who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Applying eye powder sweetens the mouth.’”
